executive_summary: This week's strategic intelligence highlights a continued push towards real-time, API-driven cash management and payments, with significant developments in ISO 20022 adoption and blockchain-based cross-border solutions. Regulatory changes, particularly PSD3 and Verification of Payee, are increasing fraud prevention obligations for PSPs, while open banking frameworks are evolving to support broader innovation. Competitors are focusing on enhancing digital platforms and leveraging programmable payments for improved corporate treasury services, especially in CEE.

market.title: SWIFT Advances Blockchain Ledger to MVP for 24/7 Cross-Border Payments
market.summary: SWIFT has moved its blockchain-based shared ledger from pilot to Minimum Viable Product (MVP) stage, aiming for live transactions by the end of 2026. This initiative seeks to enable 24/7 cross-border payments, reducing reconciliation work and liquidity uncertainty by functioning as a common digital orchestration layer on top of existing bank infrastructure. The ledger is closely linked to ISO 20022 communications and is EVM-compatible, providing control and auditability for central banks.
market.sowhat: CMIplus should monitor the progress of SWIFT's blockchain ledger MVP, especially its integration with ISO 20022. This could represent a future standard for real-time cross-border payments, potentially impacting existing H2H and correspondent banking offerings. Understanding the implications for CEE payment corridors will be crucial.

market.title: ISO 20022 Migration Continues with Focus on Structured Addresses and E&I Transformation
market.summary: The migration to CBPR+ ISO 20022 for payment instructions is largely complete, but the journey continues with upcoming requirements. From November 2026, town and country information must be provided in designated fields for all agents and parties in CBPR+ messages, with only fully structured or hybrid postal addresses accepted. Additionally, the mandate to exchange all payment cancellation messages via the Stop and Recall Process (SRP) has been postponed to November 2027, with an interim requirement in November 2026 to receive camt.110 investigation requests.
market.sowhat: CMIplus needs to ensure its platform and corporate clients are fully prepared for the stricter address structuring requirements by November 2026 to avoid payment rejections or delays. The postponement of the full E&I transformation provides a slight reprieve but emphasizes the ongoing need to prepare for ISO 20022-native exception and investigation processes.

market.title: PSD3 and PSR to Mandate Verification of Payee and Increase PSP Fraud Liability
market.summary: The proposed Payment Services Directive 3 (PSD3) and accompanying Payment Services Regulation (PSR) will significantly expand fraud refund liability for Payment Service Providers (PSPs) and mandate proactive anti-fraud measures. Verification of Payee (VoP), requiring PSPs to verify a payee's name matches the account identifier, is becoming mandatory by October 2025 for euro-area Member States. This aims to combat Authorized Push Payment (APP) scams, with instant payments heightening the challenge for real-time fraud detection.
market.sowhat: CMIplus must prioritize the implementation of robust Verification of Payee (VoP) capabilities and enhance real-time fraud detection systems to meet the upcoming PSD3 and Instant Payments Regulation requirements. This directly impacts CMIplus's compliance and risk management for instant payments in CEE, requiring potential adjustments to product features and operational workflows.

market.title: Open Banking and Embedded Finance Driving Payment Innovation
market.summary: Open banking continues to evolve, enabling consumers to share banking data with third-party providers through standardized APIs, facilitating services like account aggregation and payment initiation. Embedded finance further integrates financial products into non-financial platforms, creating new payment experiences and streamlining checkouts. This API-driven approach is seen as crucial for innovation, faster settlement times, improved cash flow, and enhanced security in payment processing.
market.sowhat: CMIplus should continue to invest in and expand its Open Banking API offerings to support embedded finance use cases for corporate clients. This trend directly aligns with CMIplus's focus on API banking and can unlock new revenue streams and enhanced client experiences, particularly for large international corporates in CEE seeking streamlined financial operations.

market.title: SWIFT Launches New Retail Payments Framework with 50+ Banks by Mid-2026
market.summary: SWIFT has announced a significant overhaul of its retail payments infrastructure with a new framework called 'Global Payments for Consumer Payments'. This initiative brings together over 50 banks across more than 25 corridors, with the first wave going live by mid-2026. The framework promises near-instant settlement, predictable fees, and full transparency for consumer transactions, covering five of the world's ten largest remittance markets.
market.sowhat: While focused on retail, this SWIFT initiative signals a broader trend towards faster, more transparent, and cost-effective payments. CMIplus should analyze how the underlying technologies and standards of this new framework might eventually influence corporate payment expectations and infrastructure, especially for instant payments and cross-border transactions in CEE.

thought.title: Core Treasury Systems Evolving with AI, Cloud, and ISO 20022 for Real-Time Operations
thought.summary: Core Treasury Systems are becoming the digital backbone of modern treasury operations, moving beyond basic tracking to centralize cash, liquidity, payments, and bank connectivity. In 2026, these systems are leveraging cloud architecture for flexibility, AI for smarter cash forecasting and fraud detection, and ISO 20022 for structured data and deeper automation. The focus is on real-time visibility and reducing manual work.
thought.sowhat: CMIplus should emphasize the integration capabilities of its platform with modern core treasury systems, highlighting how CMIplus's real-time data, API connectivity, and ISO 20022 support can enhance corporate clients' treasury transformation efforts. Exploring AI-driven features for cash forecasting and fraud detection within CMIplus's roadmap would be a strategic move.
thought.source: Core Treasury System in 2026: The Digital Backbone of Smarter Treasury Operations

thought.summary: API-driven banking is rapidly becoming the standard, replacing monolithic software with modular services. A 2024 McKinsey analysis found API-driven banks deploy new features 4.7 times faster. Oliver Wyman projects embedded finance, enabled by banking APIs, to reach $7 trillion in transaction volume by 2030, highlighting the significant growth opportunity and new revenue streams for banks through API access fees.

thought.title: Stablecoin Flows and Spillovers to FX Markets Highlight Financial Stability Concerns
thought.summary: A new working paper from the Bank for International Settlements (BIS) and the International Monetary Fund (IMF) provides evidence that stablecoin activity is impacting traditional foreign exchange (FX) markets. The research indicates that stablecoin flows can lead to depreciating local currencies and increased dollar funding costs for banks and corporates, with spillover risks potentially increasing as the stablecoin market develops.
thought.sowhat: While not directly impacting CMIplus's core offerings, the growing influence of stablecoins on FX markets and financial stability is an important trend to monitor. Philipp Hoefer should be aware of these developments as they could indirectly affect corporate treasury strategies, cross-border payment dynamics, and regulatory landscapes in the long term, particularly in CEE.
thought.source: Bank for International Settlements / Glenbrook Partners, LLC
